youtube.title: He Mailed Himself Home In A Box (True Story) 📦
youtube.description:
In October 1964, Reg Spiers, a 22-year-old Australian javelin thrower, was stuck in London with no money for a ticket home, and his daughter's birthday was coming up. He had been working in the cargo section at London's Heathrow airport, where he had seen animals shipped cash on delivery.

So his friend, the British javelin thrower John McSorley, built a wooden crate about 5 ft x 3 ft x 2.5 ft, labelled it as paint, and addressed it, cash on delivery, to a company in Perth that didn't exist. Inside: a pillow, a blanket, a torch, tinned food and two bottles, one for water and one for... later.

Fog held the Air India flight on the ground in London. In Bombay the crate sat on the tarmac in the heat, at one point upside down. About 63 hours after the lid went on, it reached Perth. He cut his way out of the crate in the cargo shed, put on his suit, walked out of the airport and hitchhiked across Australia to Adelaide, in time for his daughter's birthday.

He forgot to tell his friend he'd made it. John feared the worst and called a journalist, the story went around the world, and the airline let the bill go.

Please don't try this: it was dangerous (heat and very little air), and stowing away is illegal.

Would YOU have got in the box? 👇
